graph_notes: Dependency-aware DAG. 'depends_on' are hard blockers (must reach acceptance before start). recommended_model is a Claude model for tasks that are bounded coding/config/analysis work; tasks that require a physical device, a legal decision, a paid vendor, or a human judgment call are marked recommended_model: 'human/external' -- assigning a Claude model to those would invent a capability this audit has no evidence for.
next_recommended_task_reason: Every other branch of the DAG (CI validation, desktop packaging, PWA host testing, device QA) either depends on VS-01 directly or assumes a stable committed baseline. Right now 25 tracked files are modified and 11 paths (including the entire Electron/Steam shell, the CI workflow, and the error boundary) are untracked; nothing downstream can be trusted to survive without this triage first.

tasks.name: Golden vertical-slice hardening: triage and commit the working tree
tasks.description: 25 modified files + 11 untracked paths currently sit uncommitted (git status, captured in PROJECT_STATE.json). This includes the entire Electron/Steam desktop shell, the CI workflow, the error boundary, and RELEASE_READINESS.md/STEAM_RELEASE.md themselves. The user owns this work; this task is to review it file-by-file with the user, decide what ships, and commit it in reviewable slices (not one giant commit) so it stops being one `rm -rf` away from disappearing.
acceptance_criteria: git status shows a clean or intentionally-staged tree (no accidental untracked release-critical files)
Every committed file has been through the user's own review, not auto-committed by an agent
Commit messages describe why, matching existing repo convention (see git log style: 'area(scope): summary')
evidence: git status snapshot from this audit
tasks.risk_reason: Committing or discarding the wrong files here is destructive-adjacent (lost work) or ships unreviewed code. Not something an agent should do unattended.

tasks.name: Record the core-loop manual smoke test RELEASE_READINESS.md requires
tasks.description: RELEASE_READINESS.md's 'Core loop' exit condition ('a new player can complete tutorial -> hangar -> briefing -> flight -> results -> retry/map without a blocked screen') is explicitly a manual smoke test, not an automated one. No automated test in the 316-test suite walks this full transition graph. Perform and record it on touch and keyboard.
acceptance_criteria: A dated record exists (e.g. appended to RELEASE_READINESS.md or a QA log) of a full screen-flow run on both touch and keyboard input with no blocked screen

tasks.name: Decide the fate of the orphaned 3D asset library
tasks.description: 361 GLB files exist under public/assets/models. Exhaustive grep of every assetLibrary.load()/assetUrl() call site in src/ shows only 24 unique ids ever load at runtime (23 world props + 1 airframe, 'hero_ultralight'). 69 of 70 airframe generations, all 19 upgrade models, and all 245 micro-asset models (air_mic/env_mic/vfx) are exported, licensed as original art, and never referenced by any code path. This was not previously documented in VISUAL_DEBT.md. Needs an explicit decision, not silent scope creep: wire a subset into content (e.g. Tier 1+ frames, visible upgrades), explicitly defer with a tracked ticket, or drop from the shipping bundle if genuinely abandoned.
acceptance_criteria: Every GLB under public/assets/models is either reachable from a real content-module reference, or explicitly listed in VISUAL_DEBT.md as deferred/out-of-scope with an owner
No orphaned asset ships inside the production bundle without a documented reason (spec section 17.8: 'No placeholder may ship hidden merely because se ve suficiente')
evidence: src/render/assetManifest.ts, assetLibrary.ts, FlightScene.ts (only 2 .load() call sites in the whole codebase, both grep-verified in this audit)
tasks.risk_reason: This is a scope/product decision (what ships as content) disguised as a tech-debt cleanup; a coding agent should not unilaterally decide which of 8 aircraft generations become playable.

Screens are already route-code-split; physics/render engines are not deferred.
